decisions.reasoning: All seven occurrences denote filtered natural seawater as an input before mixing or autoclaving. CCAP MErds/NSS low require filling to one litre with it; MY75S and ZM10 explicitly dilute that input. NSS low and 2SNA allow synthetic salt alternatives, which remain separate alternatives. This scoped input is consistent with the Filtered Seawater owner; final-medium dilution and autoclaving do not turn its input label into a different source ingredient. Final-review qualification of the historical #260 dilution rationale: the original CCAP PE footnote explicitly says to filter natural seawater, reduce it to 95% using glass distilled water, and autoclave. That prepared input is then dosed at 950 cm3; the prior dilution is not inferred from the receiving-medium dose. The literal 95%-strength label is retained as REJECTED_LABEL on this bare filtered-seawater owner, without inventing the percentage basis, final volume, component ratio or a new preparation owner. The unqualified Natural seawater alias is also nonresolving: its recovered JCM1377 contexts state natural seawater without filtration. Supported Filtered natural seawater and Natural seawater (filtrated) aliases remain. Earlier #260 mapping evidence and histories are preserved as historical rationale, superseded only on these alias applicability points by this source-backed qualification. The two assigned filtered cases are not reinterpreted as the 95% preparation. Sources: https://www.ccap.ac.uk/wp-content/uploads/MR_PE.pdf ; https://www.jcm.riken.jp/cgi-bin/jcm/jcm_grmd?GRMD=1377 .

decisions.reasoning: JCM1102 explicitly lists 750 ml Natural seawater (filtrated) as an input alongside 250 ml distilled water; all four frozen TOGO variants preserve that same input while varying supplements. Filtrated and filtered name the same treatment here. The identity candidate is the existing Filtered Seawater material, not the complete anaerobic medium or its 75% dilution. Final-review qualification of the historical #260 dilution rationale: the original CCAP PE footnote explicitly says to filter natural seawater, reduce it to 95% using glass distilled water, and autoclave. That prepared input is then dosed at 950 cm3; the prior dilution is not inferred from the receiving-medium dose. The literal 95%-strength label is retained as REJECTED_LABEL on this bare filtered-seawater owner, without inventing the percentage basis, final volume, component ratio or a new preparation owner. The unqualified Natural seawater alias is also nonresolving: its recovered JCM1377 contexts state natural seawater without filtration. Supported Filtered natural seawater and Natural seawater (filtrated) aliases remain. Earlier #260 mapping evidence and histories are preserved as historical rationale, superseded only on these alias applicability points by this source-backed qualification. The two assigned filtered cases are not reinterpreted as the 95% preparation. Sources: https://www.ccap.ac.uk/wp-content/uploads/MR_PE.pdf ; https://www.jcm.riken.jp/cgi-bin/jcm/jcm_grmd?GRMD=1377 .
